alternatingChange.observation: Not blind: the historical baseline and numerical outcome are known. The sparse upper part of band1 at2500 becomes a broad branching vertical cluster at3000. Scattered lower band1 fragments expand into a longer branching arrangement, and new occupied clusters appear in lower band0. These are occupied-tile and gap changes, not color changes.

seasonalChanges.observation: Not blind: the historical baseline and numerical outcome are known. In the numerically qualifying block, the dense upper-left and lower-left clusters in band0 largely clear, leaving small isolated bodies and broad gaps. The fed band1 gains broad upper-edge and lower-edge branching clusters plus a large middle-lower cluster. This is simultaneous visible growth in band1 and retreat in band0.

Not blind: the historical baseline and numerical outcome are known. The dense upper and lower band1 clusters clear into sparse fragments. Band0 also loses occupied area overall and does not show the required20-tile gain; the numerical seasonal block fails. Visible collapse alone is not the frozen growth-and-retreat pass.
